html:
Confucius, born Kong Qiu, was a Chinese teacher and thinker of the 6th and 5th centuries BCE whose sayings shaped Chinese ethics, family life and government for over two thousand years.

He was born around 551 BCE in the state of Lu, in a time of disorder late in the Zhou dynasty. He held minor offices, then for some years travelled between states looking for a ruler who would put his ideas into practice. None did. He returned home and taught, and died around 479 BCE.

He said he was a transmitter, not a creator: he wanted to revive the values of the early Zhou. His main ideas:

  • Rulers should govern by virtue and example, not by force and punishment.
  • Ren, humaneness, is the highest virtue; li, ritual and proper conduct, gives it form.
  • Filial piety, respect for parents and ancestors, is the root of a good society.
  • Each person should act rightly in their role: ruler and subject, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger.
  • "Do not do to others what you do not want done to yourself."

His sayings were collected by his students in the Analects. Later thinkers, above all Mencius, built on them.

His influence came after his death. Emperor Wu of Han made his teaching the basis of state learning, and the classics linked to him became the core of the imperial examinations that chose officials until 1905. Confucianism spread to Korea, Japan and Vietnam, and still shapes ideas of family, education and authority across East Asia.

His contemporary in tradition, Laozi, offered the main rival vision.
sum: Confucius, born Kong Qiu, was a Chinese teacher and thinker of the 6th and 5th centuries BCE whose sayings shaped Chinese ethics, family life and government for over two thousand years.
